uncited: Hardware-based Direct Volume Ray Casting offloads the computationally intensive tasks of ray casting, shading, and compositing to dedicated programmable Digital Signal Processors (DSPs), decoupling these operations from general-purpose processors and geometry units.
The method processes volume data in a pipeline where a geometry unit generates sample data, which is then consumed by DSPs for ray casting.
**Data Transmission:** The geometry unit transmits sample density and gradient values to the ray-casting units over a dedicated bus.
**Buffering:** DSPs receive these values from an asynchronous FIFO buffer.
**DSP Processing:** Each DSP computes the interaction of light and material for each volume element.
**Result Collection:** A local master CPU collects all scanlines from the DSP memories and transfers the final image results to the host system.
The method was developed as part of the VIRIM (Volume Image Rendering on Massively Parallel Systems) project.
